scene: SKIP: duplicate of bijvoeglijke-naamwoorden:dichtbij
must: the pointing hand and a stool touching the person's shoe.
avoid: a stool far along the ground line (daar); an arm held out level toward a distant object (daar); a person sitting on the stool (not the card); two stools side by side (not a pair).
contrast: Pair with daar. The only difference is the stool: touching the person's shoe here, far down the ground line there.
example_nl: Je tas staat hier, naast de stoel.
example_en: Your bag is here, next to the chair.
alt: Een man wijst met zijn vinger naar een kruk die tegen zijn schoen staat.

scene: SKIP: duplicate of bijvoeglijke-naamwoorden:ver
must: an outstretched arm and a small stool at the end of a long empty line.
avoid: a stool at the person's feet (hier); a stool drawn small because it is a toy (klein); a person walking toward it (not the card); a pointing hand with no object (not the card).
contrast: Pair with hier. The only difference is the stool: far down the empty ground line here, touching the person's shoe there.
example_nl: Daar staat mijn auto, bij de boom.
example_en: My car is over there, by the tree.
alt: Een man strekt zijn arm uit naar een kleine kruk aan het eind van een lange lege weg.

scene: SKIP: duplicate of voorzetselpaden:binnen-onder-de-parasol
must: the person drawn inside the cutaway walls.
avoid: a person standing in front of the shut door (buiten); a person on the roof (boven); a person at an open door (naar binnen); a person looking out of the window (not the card).
contrast: Pair with buiten. The only difference is where the adult stands: inside the cutaway walls here, on the empty ground in front of the door there.
example_nl: Het is koud, dus wij blijven binnen.
example_en: It is cold, so we stay inside.
alt: Een man staat in een kamer van een klein huis, naast een stoel.

scene: SKIP: duplicate of voorzetselpaden:buiten-in-de-tuin
must: the person on the ground in front of the house while the room is empty.
avoid: a person in the room (binnen); a person at the open door stepping out (naar buiten); a person under an umbrella in rain (not the card); a person standing on the roof (boven).
contrast: Pair with binnen. The only difference is where the adult stands: on the empty ground in front of the door here, inside the cutaway room there.
example_nl: De kinderen spelen buiten in de tuin.
example_en: The children are playing outside in the garden.
alt: Een man staat voor een gesloten deur bij een struik; de kamer erachter is leeg.

scene: SKIP: duplicate of bijvoeglijke-naamwoorden:gezellig
must: two people at one table facing each other.
avoid: one person at the table with an empty chair (alleen); two people sitting back to back (not the card); two separate tables (apart); a crowd at a long table (veel).
contrast: Pair with alleen-solo. The only difference is the second person: seated across the table here, an empty pushed-in chair there.
example_nl: Wij werken vandaag samen aan de tafel.
example_en: We are working together at the table today.
alt: Twee mensen zitten tegenover elkaar aan een tafel met elk een kop.

scene: SKIP: duplicate of bijvoeglijke-naamwoorden:eenzaam
must: one person at the table with an empty chair opposite.
avoid: two people sitting at the table (samen); a person sitting with a sad face (not the card); a person in an empty room (not the frame); a table with no chairs (not the card).
contrast: Pair with samen. The only difference is the second chair: empty and pushed in here, taken by a second person there.
alt: Een vrouw zit aan een tafel met een kop; de stoel tegenover haar is leeg.

scene: Two children of the same height stand side by side, whole-figure, facing the viewer, and each holds one plain round balloon on a string in the raised hand, the two balloons floating at equal height above their heads. The wall behind is plain.
must: both children holding a balloon at equal height.
avoid: one child holding a balloon and the other with empty hands (alleen-enkel); two children holding two different objects (not the pair); one child holding two balloons (veel); a single child (not the frame).
contrast: Pair with alleen-enkel. The only difference is the second child's hand: holding a balloon here, empty there.
example_nl: Ik wil ook een kopje koffie.
example_en: I want a cup of coffee too.
alt: Twee kinderen staan naast elkaar en houden elk een ballon boven hun hoofd.

scene: Two children of the same height stand side by side, whole-figure, facing the viewer. Only the child on the left holds one plain round balloon on a string in the raised hand; the other child's raised hand is open and empty. The wall behind is plain.
must: one balloon, held by one child only, beside an empty hand.
avoid: both children holding a balloon (ook); one child standing alone with no second child (alleen-solo); a child holding the balloon and handing it over (not the card); a child with a sad face (not the card).
contrast: Pair with ook. The only difference is the second child's hand: empty here, holding a balloon there.
example_nl: Alleen mijn zus heeft een fiets.
example_en: Only my sister has a bike.
alt: Twee kinderen staan naast elkaar; één houdt een ballon omhoog en de ander heeft een lege hand.

scene: One plain table lamp with a round shade on a small plain table, seen from the front, shining: bold straight rays leave the shade in all directions and a ring of light lies on the table. A plain wall is behind and the cord runs to the floor.
must: bold rays leaving the lamp shade.
avoid: a lamp with no rays (uit); a lamp in a dark room (donker); a broken lamp with a cracked shade (kapot); a candle (not the card).
contrast: Pair with uit. The only difference is the lamp: rays and a ring of light here, plain shade and no rays there.
example_nl: De lamp in de kamer is aan.
example_en: The lamp in the room is on.
alt: Een lamp op een tafel met strepen die van de kap af stralen.

scene: One plain table lamp with a round shade on a small plain table, seen from the front, with no rays and no light ring at all; only the plain outline of the shade is drawn. The cord runs down to the floor as before, and the plain wall behind and the table are unchanged.
must: a plain lamp shade with no rays at all.
avoid: a lamp with rays (aan); a lamp drawn in a dark scene (donker); a lamp that is cracked (kapot); an empty table with no lamp (not the card).
contrast: Pair with aan. The only difference is the lamp: no rays and no light ring here, bold rays there.
example_nl: Doe de lamp uit, het is laat.
example_en: Turn the lamp off, it is late.
alt: Een lamp op een tafel geeft geen licht; er komen geen strepen van de kap.

scene: The small plain house with its front wall cut away, at the left edge: one adult in plain clothes sits relaxed on a plain sofa in the room, a plain shoulder bag hanging on a hook on the wall, and the road to the right edge is empty.
must: a person sitting on a sofa inside the cutaway house, bag on its hook.
avoid: a person walking on the road with a bag (onderweg); a person in front of the house (buiten); a person asleep in bed (not the card); a person at a desk working (not the card).
contrast: Pair with onderweg. The only difference is where the adult is: seated in the room with the bag on the wall hook here, walking on the road with the bag there.
example_en: My father is at home now.
alt: Een man zit op een bank in een kamer; zijn tas hangt aan de muur.

scene: The small plain house with its front wall cut away stands at the left edge, its sofa empty and its wall hook bare. One adult in plain clothes walks on the plain road toward the right with the plain shoulder bag on the shoulder, mid-stride, the house clearly behind and the road ahead.
must: a person mid-stride on the road with a bag, the house behind.
avoid: a person sitting in the room (thuis); a person standing at the door (buiten); a person running with speed lines (snel); a person on a bus (not the card).
contrast: Pair with thuis. The only difference is where the adult is: walking on the road with the bag on the shoulder here, seated in the room there.
example_nl: Ik ben onderweg naar mijn werk.
example_en: I am on the way to my work.
alt: Een man loopt met een tas over een weg; het huis staat achter hem.

scene: A plain flat tray on the plain wooden table holds about fifteen whole round apples lying close together and filling the tray, several touching. The wall behind is plain and nothing else is on the table.
must: a tray crowded with a great many apples.
avoid: a tray with only two apples (weinig); a basket heaped over the rim (genoeg, te veel); one huge apple (groot); a single row of apples (not the card).
contrast: Pair with weinig. The only difference is the number of apples: about fifteen filling the tray here, two lost on the tray there.
example_nl: Er staan veel mensen op straat.
example_en: There are many people in the street.
alt: Een dienblad op een tafel ligt vol met ronde appels.

scene: A plain flat tray on the plain wooden table holds just two whole round apples, one near each end and far apart, leaving most of the tray bare. The wall behind is plain and nothing else is on the table.
must: a tray that is mostly bare with only two apples.
avoid: a tray crowded with apples (veel); an empty tray with no apples (leeg); one tiny apple (klein); two apples on a very small plate (not the frame).
contrast: Pair with veel. The only difference is the number of apples: two on a mostly bare tray here, about fifteen filling it there.
alt: Op een dienblad liggen maar twee appels, ver uit elkaar.

scene: Three adults sit side by side at the long plain table seen from the front, hands resting on the table, and in front of each adult stands exactly one plain cup, three cups in all, one for each person. The wall behind is plain and nothing else is on the table.
must: one cup in front of each of the three people.
avoid: seven cups crowding the table (te veel); two cups for three people (te weinig); a table with no cups (leeg); one huge cup (groot).
contrast: Pair with te-veel. The only difference is the number of cups: three, one for each person, here; seven crowding the table there.
example_nl: Dit brood is genoeg voor ons allemaal.
example_en: This bread is enough for all of us.
alt: Drie mensen zitten naast elkaar aan een tafel; voor elk van hen staat één kopje.

scene: Three adults sit side by side at the long plain table seen from the front, hands resting on the table, and seven plain cups crowd the table in front of them, more than two for each adult, several touching. The wall behind is plain and nothing else is on the table.
must: seven cups crowding the table in front of three people.
avoid: one cup for each person (genoeg); a table with no cups (leeg); cups stacked in a tall pile (hoog); a crowd of people at the table (not the frame).
contrast: Pair with genoeg. The only difference is the number of cups: seven crowding the table here; three, one for each person, there.
example_nl: Dat is te veel voor mij.
example_en: That is too much for me.
alt: Drie mensen zitten naast elkaar aan een tafel met zeven kopjes voor zich.

scene: SKIP: duplicate of bijvoeglijke-naamwoorden:vol
must: water exactly level with the rim and no gap.
avoid: water a finger below the rim with the jug still pouring (bijna); a glass with only a thin layer (een beetje); water spilling over the rim (te veel); a glass with no water (leeg).
contrast: Pair with bijna and beetje. The only difference is the water level: right up to the rim here, a finger below it with the jug pouring in bijna, a thin layer in beetje.
alt: Een glas staat op tafel met water tot aan de rand; de kan staat ernaast.

scene: SKIP: duplicate of bijvoeglijke-naamwoorden:vol
must: a visible small gap between the water line and the rim, with a stream still falling.
avoid: water exactly level with the rim (helemaal); only a thin layer of water (een beetje); water spilling over (te veel); a half full glass (half).
contrast: Pair with helemaal and beetje. The only difference is the water level: a finger below the rim with a stream still pouring here, right up to the rim in helemaal, a thin layer in beetje.
alt: Een kan giet water in een glas; er is nog een klein stukje ruimte bovenaan.

scene: SKIP: duplicate of bijvoeglijke-naamwoorden:vol
must: just a thin layer of water in the bottom of the glass.
avoid: a glass filled to the rim (helemaal); a glass nearly full with a stream pouring (bijna); a completely empty glass (leeg); a drop on the table (not the card).
contrast: Pair with helemaal and bijna. The only difference is the water level: a thin layer here, up to the rim in helemaal, a finger below it with the jug pouring in bijna.
alt: Een glas staat op tafel met een dun laagje water op de bodem.

scene: The plain brick wall stands complete on the flat ground line, seen from the side, with a flat even top along its whole length and no loose bricks anywhere. The adult stands upright beside it holding the trowel in one hand. The ground beside the wall is bare.
must: a complete wall with a flat top and no bricks left over.
avoid: a half-built wall with a stepped top and a brick pile (bezig); a crumbling wall (kapot); a very tall wall (hoog); a person resting on a bench (not the card).
contrast: Pair with bezig. The only difference is the wall: complete with a flat top and no bricks left here, half built with a stepped top and a brick pile there.
alt: Een man staat naast een muur met een vlakke bovenkant; er liggen geen stenen meer.

scene: The plain brick wall stands half built on the flat ground line, seen from the side, its top rising in steps, and a small pile of loose bricks lies beside it. The adult stands upright beside it holding the trowel in one hand, exactly as beside the finished wall.
must: a half-built wall with a stepped top and a pile of bricks beside it.
avoid: a complete wall with a flat top and no bricks (af); a broken wall with fallen bricks (kapot); a person sleeping on the bricks (not the card); an empty building site (leeg).
contrast: Pair with af. The only difference is the wall: half built with a stepped top and a brick pile here, complete with a flat top and no bricks left there.
example_nl: Ik ben bezig met mijn huiswerk.
example_en: I am busy with my homework.
alt: Een man staat naast een halve muur met een trapvormige bovenkant; ernaast ligt een stapel stenen.
